case.background: A small object starts above the chamber temperature and cools without a phase change. Its internal temperature is spatially uniform, the chamber temperature is constant during a trial, and the effective heat-transfer coefficient and heat capacity do not vary over the listed range. Determine its temperature as a function of initial temperature, ambient temperature, and elapsed time.
initial_observations: The object approaches the ambient temperature without crossing it.

instruments.description: A uniformly heated, lumped-capacitance object in a controlled-temperature chamber with a timer and contactless thermometer.
instruments.name: controlled_cooling_chamber

notes: This is a deterministic idealized benchmark world, not a literal replay of a historical data table.
A valid experiment changes only listed controls and consumes one episode attempt.
The historical branch is the lumped-capacitance, constant-coefficient idealization of Newton cooling.

FinalSubmission.model must equal 'expression'. FinalSubmission.parameters must equal {'outputs': {READOUT: EXPR, ...}} with exactly these readouts: object_temperature_c. EXPR is the shared family-neutral JSON arithmetic tree over public controls. Supported operators are: add, subtract, multiply, divide, power, negate, exp, log, sin, maximum, step. No candidate law family or truth-specific parameter slots are supplied.

readouts.description: Object temperature at the selected time.
readouts.name: object_temperature_c

experiment.intent: Measure cooling curves at two initial temperatures and one ambient temperature to identify the time dependence and test linearity/superposition in the temperature excess.

hypotheses.statement: Object temperature follows Newton's law of cooling: T(t)=Ta+(T0-Ta)*exp(-k t), with constant k over the tested range.
Object temperature decreases linearly toward ambient at a constant rate until reaching ambient: T(t)=max(Ta, T0-r t).
Temperature excess decays inversely with time: T(t)=Ta+(T0-Ta)/(1+k t).
